note: Hand-run LIKE-FOR-LIKE measurements of the locked stage header, and the PRODUCT targets derived from them. Numbers only: the reference images are private design inputs and are not copied into the tree. METHOD (one function on every image): the INK of an element = the bounding box of the pixels whose largest channel difference from the most common colour of the measured rectangle exceeds 40 (scratch/hdr/header_elems.mjs in the evidence; the test measures the product the same way on a viewport screenshot, inside each element's own DOM box grown by 2 px). EXCEPTION: the Mission details BACK BOX (back.top, back.left, back.w, back.h) is the earlier pass's HAND measurement of the lock (left 296, right 342, top 28, bottom 79), NOT an ink-function measurement, and the product's Mission Back box is measured as its OUTER LAYOUT RECTANGLE: layout-box geometry against hand-measured reference bounds, not ink against ink. Its painted ring is checked separately by the rule under views.mission.paint. All values are image pixels = CSS pixels at device pixel ratio 1. POSITIONS ARE RELATIVE TO THE STAGE'S OWN LEFT EDGE (the first column after its border): the locks keep a world strip left of the stage (the recorded D-2 'rail priority' deviation), so absolute x cannot be compared. LOCK COLUMN = what the reference draws; TARGET COLUMN = what the product is required to measure: they differ only where a recorded decision says so (the NOTE). Below 1500 px there is NO reference for Code Diff and Mission details: their sizes are DERIVED (about 0.72 of these) and are not asserted here; Comments' reference is measured at 1280 and applies as measured. `scales: true` marks the numbers that the stylesheet derives below 1500 px as about 0.72 of the value here (diScanHeaderGeometry.test.ts asserts that CONSISTENCY at 1280 x 720, labelled DERIVED: it is not a reference). Back's own size and Mission details' band padding have their own compact rules and do not scale.

In the lock the shape SELECTED by the violet colour predicate (b - g > 40 and b > 120) is 35 rows high, and the ink function (a pixel differing from the background by more than 40) also takes a top row of three faint non-violet pixels, so the lock's INK box is 36 high (logs/mark-lock02-dump-20261028T051612Z.log). The product draws the SELECTED shape as its OWN Mission-only drawing (45 x 35; never the 45 x 29 asset stretched), so it measures 35 and PASSES 36 +-1 ONLY ON THE TOLERANCE EDGE, which is where it sits; the target and the tolerance are not changed (the Supervisor, round 26). The violet selection is a colour threshold on a raster: it does not establish the original artwork's opacity or vector boundary, and the 36 is what the ink function measures on the lock, not demonstrably what the lock draws
